A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research, renamed from FUSION to FLARE. Their main texts, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison. Changed experimental configurations require care when comparing scores.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark evaluations, component and training ablations, token-reduction experiments, and ConvBench multi-turn dialogue results.

after.justification: V3 reports original benchmark evaluations, controlled model comparisons, computational measurements, parameter ablations, and human/GPT-4o evaluations of synthetic data.

M1.justification: V1 Section 3.2 constructs separately encoded, text-independent auxiliary image features and initializes latent tokens by interpolation. V3 uses the projected image tokens directly as attention keys/values and specifies randomly initialized latent tokens. It also introduces crop-wise processing for dynamic resolution. These revise the decoding procedure despite retaining the overall framework and reconstruction losses.

E1.justification: V3 removes ConvBench multi-turn evaluation and the HallusionBench, MME-RealWorld, and DocVQA benchmark results. DocVQA remains training data; VizWiz and LLaVA-Wild remain in appendix ablations. Appendix E.3 adds an image/text quality assessment task comparing synthetic and existing datasets. The extensive training-data mixture largely persists.

E2.justification: Within Table 1, v3 adds MiniCPM variants and Molmo-7B, removes InternVL2 and MM1.5, and replaces Qwen2VL-7B with Qwen2.5VL-7B. Molmo and Qwen2.5VL already appeared in v1's broader appendix comparison. V3 also expands controlled architectural comparisons beyond LLaVA-NeXT to Florence-VL, Cambrian-1, and Eagle.

E3.justification: V3 evaluates fixed-resolution FLARE-L and dynamic-resolution FLARE-X, adds NaViT/Qwen2.5 backbone experiments and matched-data comparisons, and changes latent-token sampling from {4,16,64,144,256} to {4,16,36,64,144}. New data-quality evaluations score 50 random examples per dataset on a 0–10 scale. Reported image-generation steps change from 60 to 50; this does not establish that earlier experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V3 adds exchange-layer placement/count sweeps, reconstruction-loss weight sweeps, computational profiling, and synthetic-data quality and distribution analyses. V1's window-size study, latent-only versus interaction-layer control, inference-token compression studies, and ConvBench analysis disappear. Latent-sampling and parameter-freezing studies remain, while the snowboard/person attention visualization is relocated rather than newly added.

E5.justification: V3 Section 4 newly specifies seed 42 for training and evaluation. This is additional seed disclosure, not evidence of more runs. Neither version reports repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or statistical significance testing.

E6.justification: Main benchmark and component-ablation results are extensively revised, with additional controlled-comparison, compute, and data-quality results. For example, v1 Table 9 reports MMBench-EN 80.3 for FUSION-X 3B at 630 tokens; v3 Table 1 reports 79.6 for FLARE-L 3B at 630 and 81.4 for FLARE-X 3B at approximately 1400. These concern revised models/settings, not established same-setting gains or losses. ConvBench and compression result entries are removed.

T1.justification: The decoder's mathematical specification changes from square patches of an interpolated auxiliary representation to rectangular slices of projected image tokens, with window dimensions defined by w=m/l and h=n/l. Feature aggregation, reconstruction losses, and SSIM/CLIP filtering formulas remain substantively equivalent. Neither version develops theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The four central contributions and full-pipeline integration claim remain. V3 explicitly extends the claimed model family to fixed and dynamic resolution and emphasizes computational efficiency. V1's specific claim that the 3B model surpasses Cambrian-1 8B even at approximately 300 tokens is removed.

C2.justification: V3 newly attributes higher synthetic-data CLIPScores partly to filtering, acknowledges poorer generated-image quality, and discusses distribution gaps involving ScienceQA. It also adds interpretations of loss-weight and exchange-layer sensitivity. Conversely, v1's substantive discussion of initial-question encoding bias in multi-turn dialogue and its proposed compensation mechanism is removed.

D1.justification: V3 newly discloses one-epoch training on 64 A100 GPUs, exchange-layer insertion every three decoder layers, initialization details, and hardware for compute measurements. It specifies FLUX-dev and the description/QA generation model. V1's explicit 256-token text cap and 1024×1024 generation resolution are no longer documented. Most synthesis prompts and filtering thresholds are retained.

R1.justification: V3 adds MiniCPM-V and newer data/reasoning references while removing substantial earlier citation coverage. More substantively, it removes Question Aware Vision Transformer for Multimodal Reasoning: v1 Section 3.1 explicitly credits this work as inspiration, whereas v3 presents the encoding contribution without that relationship. This changes attribution and positioning of a central component beyond bibliographic restyling.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and method explanations undergo extensive rewriting and condensation, alongside model/component renaming and revised notation. Data-collection material moves into the main paper, the experimental narrative is reorganized, and the appendices gain reproducibility and LLM-use statements. Most detailed synthesis prompts remain unchanged.

P2.justification: V3 changes the two-column presentation to a single-column conference format and consolidates the main benchmark table. It removes the opening performance plot and token-compression plots, adds loss curves, t-SNE plots, and comparison/compute tables, and relocates alignment and dataset-composition figures. Architecture diagrams are relabeled; synthetic-example Figures 10–19 retain their content.

improvement.justification: V3 substantially strengthens support for the central architecture and efficiency claims: Table 4 controls the LLM and training data across several baselines, Tables 5–6 measure computational cost directly, and Appendix E.3 evaluates synthetic-data quality and acknowledges weaknesses. These address important comparison and validation gaps in v1. Removing multi-turn/compression evidence, the associated limitation discussion, and the earlier encoder attribution weakens breadth and transparency, but the stronger controlled evidence provides a substantial net improvement.
